HomeEssentials Retail - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Retail Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Retail's results for the Q3 FY2024. Joining me on today’s call are Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Vargas, Chief Merchandising Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Retail's performance for the Q3 FY2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover five key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We achieved comparable store sales growth of 3.2%, driven by a balanced mix of traffic increases and resilient basket sizes in our core home essentials categories, while reaffirming our full-year guidance amid stable GDP growth and category tailwinds.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital channels contributed 23% of sales, up from 19% last year, with buy-online-pick-up-in-store fulfillment at 28% of online orders powering 40% of the comp lift through ship-from-store efficiency.

3. Store Performance: Our 1,200 stores saw regional strength, particularly in the Sun Belt with 5% comps from new openings and remodels, offset by softer Northeast traffic, as we optimize our portfolio with 25 openings and targeted closures.

4. Marketing Initiatives: We ramped investments in high-ROI digital channels, achieving better ROAS through targeted social and search, while leveraging vendor co-ops to drive traffic and loyalty.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Efficiencies reduced costs as a percentage of sales and improved inventory turns to 7.2x, thanks to AI forecasting and automation across our DCs.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 FY2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $3.25 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year, aligning with our reaffirmed full-year outlook.

Gross margin was 38.5%, expanding 120 basis points year-over-year. Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—as a leading brick-and-mortar retailer with over 1,200 stores across the U.S. and Canada, specializing in home essentials, appliances, and seasonal goods, much like peers at Home Depot and Target, we're pleased with this resilient outcome in a softening consumer setting. This marks our strongest Q3 gross margin since pre-pandemic 2019 levels. To contextualize, last year's Q3 stood at 37.3%, weighed down by sky-high ocean freight at around $12,000 per container—300% above 2019 averages—and supply bottlenecks that pushed us toward costlier spot market purchases for items like lumber and textiles. This quarter, we recaptured that through targeted actions, generating $185 million more in gross profit dollars even as comps moderated slightly.

Product mix shift accounted for about 70 basis points of the gain. We shifted toward stronger-margin areas, with home décor and our private-label apparel now at 28% of sales, versus 22% a year ago. Our Essentials Own private label—affordable kitchenware and bedding similar to Walmart's Mainstays—posted segment margins of 48%, compared to 35% for national brands. This echoes TJX's off-price model success. Seasonal patio and outdoor living comped up 4%, lifting average unit margins by 2.2 points, while we dialed back on lower-margin basics like towels.

Pricing discipline and promotion tweaks added another 50 basis points. With deflation in big-ticket goods—lumber down 15% per Random Lengths—we stuck to everyday low pricing and raised gift-with-purchase bars. Full-price sell-through reached 72%, up from 65%, powered by our AI dynamic pricing tool like Macy's Dynamic Yield setup. Markdowns dropped to 11.8% of sales from 14.2%, sidestepping the clearance traps that hurt Bed Bath & Beyond. We passed on 60% of input cost savings to shoppers, maintaining value perception.

Supply chain and COGS improvements contributed 40 basis points. Freight plunged 22% year-over-year to $4.2 million or 85 basis points of sales, with ocean rates at $3,200 per FEU as Red Sea issues eased via rerouting. Nearshoring now covers 35% of apparel from Mexico and Central America, up from 18%, trimming lead times 25 days and duties under USMCA. Shrink fell 30 basis points to 1.4% of sales via RFID across 80% of big-box stores, targeting 100% by year-end, curbing organized retail crime like at Dollar General. COGS per unit eased 4.1%, beating the 2.8% revenue per unit dip.

By region, Northeast stores—35% of footprint—led with 180 basis point expansion to 41.1%, from winter replen into spring like HVAC filters and mulch. Midwest gained 120 basis points steadily. Southeast, hit by hurricanes in Florida and Gulf—20% of stores—managed 90 basis points to 37.5% amid $12 million storm shrink and rush freight. Canada, 15% of sales, jumped 160 basis points to 38.9% via weak CAD on U.S. goods.

These wins highlight our store-first, tech-enabled strategy, with $150 million in backroom automation like Swisslog goods-to-person systems—akin to Lowe's—hitting 98.5% fulfillment accuracy and BOPIS margins 500 basis points over pure e-comm. Ahead, Q4 gross margin eyes 39.0-39.5%, full-year up 100-120 basis points, assuming steady freight and no tariff jumps on our 15% China imports. Watch cotton volatility—up 8% quarter-over-quarter per ICAC—or discounter price fights like Big Lots. This sets us to leverage SG&A while funding 150 urban new stores next year.

Operating expenses were $820 million, representing 25.2% of revenue. Within that, marketing and advertising trends merit a spotlight—they totaled $152 million, up 8% year-over-year or 3.2% of sales, a slight uptick from Q1's 5% rise. This reflects our pivot to higher-return digital in a macro with sticky inflation, softer discretionary sentiment, and e-tailer pressure from Amazon and Wayfair.

Breaking it out: Digital took 68% of budget, up from 55% last year and 62% in Q1—$85 million on paid search, social, programmatic, and CTV. Traditional TV, radio, OOH fell to 22% or $33 million, down 15%. Co-op, in-store, sponsorships steady at 10% or $14 million.

Digital efficiencies shone: Google/Meta led, search ROAS to 4.8x from 4.2x via first-party data post-iOS shifts. Performance Max targeted 'affordable sectionals under $1,000,' hiking impression share 12% at $1.85 CPC. Meta/TikTok up 25% to $28 million on shoppable remodel videos, CPA to $22 for loyalty sign-ups from $28.

Programmatic and our Retail Media Network got $18 million via Trade Desk, partnering P&G/Whirlpool for app/BOPIS placements—$45 million extra vendor sales at 6x ROAS. CTV on Hulu/Roku boosted Sunbelt patio traffic 14%.

U.S. (75% spend): Sunbelt up 4% spend for 18% traffic via geofencing around 250 small-format stores and migration-tied campaigns. Northeast up 12% for sluggish traffic, TV/OOH on 'Essentials' bundles holding AOV at $145 amid 3% deflation.

Ex-U.S. $22 million up 10%: UK/Germany omnichannel retargeting via Criteo at 22% higher conversions; India/SEA TikTok/Jio at $8 CPA, 30% acquisition growth via influencers for bedding.

This 'Efficient Growth' cuts CAC 11% to $35, lifts loyalty CLV to $1,250 from $1,150 with Adobe personalization. Axed print circulars saved $8 million; kiosks boost SMS opt-ins 25%. Vendor co-op at 28% of spend.

Q4 spend up 6-8% to $155-160 million, front-loading holidays with $40 million Black Friday omnichannel. ML models eye 15-20% ROAS uplift. This fuels 7% comps vs. peers like Macy's struggles.

Net income was $165 million, or $0.75 per share. We generated $275 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently optimized at 12 weeks' cover, down from 14 weeks last year.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

One more highlight before passing to Lisa: our supply chain efficiencies. Year-over-year, costs as a percentage of sales dropped 15.2% to 10.9%. Inventory turns rose to 7.2x from 5.8x, cutting days on hand to 48 from 66—beating NRF's 5.5x home goods benchmark and nearing Home Depot's 6.9x—without stockouts over 1.2% in appliances, bedding, décor amid 4.1% comps.

AI demand sensing with Blue Yonder hit 92% accuracy from 84%, blending POS from 1,250 stores with housing starts, confidence data—slashing excess inventory 22%, especially furniture.

Capex of $180 million automated 28 DCs: 450 Locus AMRs in top 10 boosted picks 35% to 350/hour; Dallas mega-DC's Dematic AS/RS cut labor 28% for 15% more volume. RFID at 85% cut receiving errors 40%.

North America (78% throughput): Asia ocean freight down 12% via negotiations, 25% more Mexico hardlines at Otay Mesa—dwell 3.2 days vs. 7 industry. Europe (15%) up 9% despite Brexit; Manchester micro-DC for 200 stores hits 96% BOPIS under 2 hours. Asia-Pac 8% gain post-Typhoon via Vietnam textiles, 15-day shorter leads.

Transportation down 17% to $285 million with 1,200-trailer ORION routing—12% MPG gain, 20% less deadhead. 40% electric/CNG fleet cuts Scope 3 14%, earns rebates, lifts NPS 3 points.

FY25's $120 million adds Manhattan WMS, blockchain private-label trace, 150 store-hubs—targeting 10-12% more cuts, 200 bps gross expansion for buybacks.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Vargas, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

Lisa Vargas, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Michael. This quarter, we launched our expanded Essentials Home private label line, which has seen exceptional traction—now 42% of assortments, delivering mid-single-digit comps in décor and appliances, 500 basis points margin better than nationals, and strong uptake via our app's 18 million Rewards members. We're excited about the potential of this and upcoming launches like modular furniture and VR design zones.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Johnathan Reed:
Good morning, John. Inflation remains sticky, particularly in food-away-from-home, making consumers value-conscious, but our essentials focus—70% recession-resistant—with private-label growth to 42% has kept basket sizes resilient at +1-2%, core categories like décor and appliances delivering mid-single digits, outpacing peers like Target amid similar pressures.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Doe with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Jane. For Q4 ending January 31, 2025, we project SSS at 2.5% to 4.5%, weighted to core home décor and small appliances in mid-single digits via RFID cutting out-of-stocks 22%, while seasonal hits 1-3% given value focus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Johnathan Reed:
Absolutely, Mike. We've accelerated across the board: turns to 7.2x, 48 days inventory via Blue Yonder AI at 92% forecast accuracy; AMRs and AS/RS slashing labor 28%; nearshoring and RFID for visibility. Costs down 15% to sales, positioning us for holiday agility unlike peers struggling with disruptions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Barclays):
Thanks. On guidance, can you walk through the key assumptions for FY2025?

Michael Chen:
Sure, Emily. Before Q&A fully opens, let me cover our forward-looking guidance and underpinnings. For Q4 FY2024: net sales $2.85-2.95 billion, 4-7% growth including 2% from 15 net new stores in Sun Belt pilots at 80k sq ft with 150 bps comp uplift. SSS 2.5-4.5%; gross margin 38.0-38.8%, up 50-130 bps from freight down 15%, private label 42%, AI shrink cuts 18%. Adj op income $285-315M, EBITDA 12.5-13.2%; SG&A 25.2-25.7%; EPS $0.85-0.98 at 25.5% tax, 220M shares.

For FY2025: sales $11.9-12.3B, 3-6% growth with 50-60 net stores including urban formats. SSS 2-4%, Northeast low end, Southeast/West high via remodels/VR lifting ticket $45. Gross 37.8-38.5% with 100 bps from 55% domestic sourcing; op margin 7.5-8.2%; capex $450-500M on remodels, DCs, IT; EPS $3.45-3.75 with productivity/loyalty boosts.

Assumptions: GDP 2-2.3%, durable spending 1.5-2.5%, CPI 2.4-2.6%; bifurcated consumer trading to private label 28%; comps split traffic +1-2%, units +1%, ticket +1%; category core +3-5%, furniture flat-2%, seasonal +4-6%; e-comm 22-24%. Gross +25-65 bps from AI pricing, freight $2500/FEU, nearshoring 45%; SG&A leverage to 32.8-33% with labor +3.5%, marketing 4:1 ROI; Sunbelt +5-7% comps, portfolio flat sq ft net; inventory $1.8B 14 weeks, capex $350-375M, FCF $400-450M.

Embeds resilient essentials, risks like high rates, tariffs, wages; upside remodels/e-comm. Positions us to outperform.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes our Q&A session for now.

Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

FY2025: sales $11.9-12.3B (3-6% growth), SSS 2-4%, gross margin 37.8-38.5%, op margin 7.5-8.2%, EPS $3.45-3.75. Full-year FY2024 guidance reaffirmed.
